what_this_is: Per-pose estimate of how far each reference crop is from a true side-on view of the PISTOL (not of the character). Angle phi = angle between the gun's long axis and the image plane. phi=0 is a true orthographic side view; phi=90 would be muzzle-on.
sheet: ../jinx-i2t/ref/pose_gun_5view.jpg  (3000x1462). Crops located in it by exact template match, correlation 1.0000.

method.principle: For a body of revolution under projection, the silhouette width MEASURED PERPENDICULAR TO THE PROJECTED AXIS equals the true diameter and is not foreshortened, while any distance ALONG the axis is foreshortened by cos(phi). So the dimensionless ratio R = (axial distance between two fixed landmarks) / (tube outside diameter) is proportional to cos(phi) and is free of both the mm/px scale and of any per-panel size change.
method.landmarks_used: muzzle rim (front-most silhouette point of the muzzle collar) and the front edge of the lattice collar (the crisp step where the copper tube meets the pierced brass sleeve). Both are high-contrast in all four crops.
method.tube_diameter_station: the plain cylindrical stretch between the mid brass band and the muzzle collar, tube only, gold top rail excluded (read from a pixel column, not from the filled silhouette, because the tube's mid-tone matches the sheet background to within 6/255 and the filled mask over-reads by ~5 px).
method.anchoring: R only fixes the RATIOS of cos(phi). It is anchored by phi(pose3)=16 deg, taken from the fact that pose3 still shows an open bore ellipse of aspect ~0.5 at the muzzle. That anchor is weak (see uncertainty).
method.falsifiable_prediction: Render the built model from any camera. Measure R the same way. R/R_max must equal cos(phi) of that camera to within 0.05.

poses.notes: Barrel points away from camera: the muzzle face is turned away, no bore visible. Gun images 16-22% SMALLER than in poses 1/3 at identical body scale - see perspective note.
Barrel points toward camera: bore open. This is the CHARACTER's true side view, but it is NOT the gun's side view - the aiming arm carries the gun ~27 deg out of the image plane.

Nearly muzzle-on. Worst pose for any axial measurement; best pose for anything about the muzzle cross-section. Landmark identification (which brass ring is the lattice front) is the least certain here, hence the larger error bar.
CLOSEST TO SIDE-ON. Use this crop for every axial and every height measurement. Its axis runs at -2.7 deg to the sheet's x axis (muzzle to the right, slightly up).

perspective_note.finding: The sheet is NOT orthographic, contrary to referenceCamera.projection='orthographic' in ../jinx-i2t/baseline/spec_baseline.json.
perspective_note.evidence: The tube outside diameter is a view-invariant under orthographic projection. Measured tube-only OD: pose0 31 px, pose1 36 px, pose2 45 px, pose3 37 px, while the five figures' pixel heights agree to 1.5% (1214/1222/1226/1232 px for panels 0-3). A 16-31% spread in gun size with a 1.5% spread in body size is what a perspective camera does when the gun swings ~0.8 m toward and away from it on the end of an extended arm, and is not something an orthographic camera can do at all.
perspective_note.implied_camera: ~3 m subject distance, ~30-35 deg vertical field of view, if the body is the declared 1.72 m.
perspective_note.consequence: Do not transfer a pixel measurement from one panel to another without renormalising by a feature measured in BOTH panels. Ratios taken inside one panel are safe; absolute px are not.
